title: Version pin policy with licensing guardrails and performance-profile certificates
creator: Anika Rao
description: Define and implement a model version pinning policy that enforces license compatibility checks during onboarding and emits performance-profile certificates that travel with pinned versions. This ticket scopes the product and API changes, required checks, and the UX for exception handling when weights or licenses are encumbered.
background: We regularly onboard community and vendor models. Some incoming artifacts include restrictive licenses or encumbered weights (e.g., limited redistribution, non-commercial). Customers need predictable serving behavior: pinned versions that are verified for license compatibility and annotated with a signed performance profile (latency/cost characteristics). Currently onboarding blocks are ad-hoc and engineering implements manual exceptions.
goals: Create a deterministic decision path for pinning a model version that includes license checks
Emit a machine-readable 'performance-profile certificate' (signed metadata) tied to a pinned version
Provide a runtime guardrail that prevents serving of pinned versions with disallowed licenses unless an approved exception exists
Surface clear UX in Console and API for exceptions and temporary pins
in_scope: API endpoint for creating a pinned version that validates license metadata
License-compatibility rules engine (first-cut ruleset) as a service
Performance-profile certificate format definition and signing workflow
Console UX: onboarding flow changes, exception request modal, and version details page showing certificate
Runtime check to block serving non-compliant pinned versions with meaningful error codes
out_of_scope: Full legal review of every license variant (we'll surface flags for Legal to review)
Automated remediation of encumbered weights without human approval
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding API rejects pin requests when license metadata maps to 'disallow-serving' in the 1.0 ruleset and returns a documented error code
Console shows a clear badge and link to license details for each pinned version

Performance-profile certificate is generated for pinned versions containing: model id, pinned sha, median inference latency (p50 for 512 tokens), tokens/sec baseline, test hardware label, and signature metadata
Runtime rejects a serve call when the pinned version lacks an accepted exception and returns error code PM_LIC_409
Exception request flow creates a ticket in Legal queue with prefilled context and retains audit trail
risks: False positives from heuristics may block safe models and slow onboarding
Overly strict enforcement could block high-value enterprise customers unless exception turnaround is fast
Complexity in signing certificates and key management if we don't coordinate with Security/KMS
dependencies: SEC-314: KMS integration for certificate signing
LEGAL-22: license ruleset and approval SLA
notes: Proposed license ruleset (first cut): allow, allow-with-attribution, require-exception, disallow-serving
Performance-profile certificate should be compact JSON signed with KMS key and stored as an attached artifact to the pinned version record
Consider exposing certificate fingerprints in API responses so downstream tooling can validate before routing traffic
